newsitem.title: UK: Scot Media to pay 105 mln stg for Grampian.
newsitem.headline: Scot Media to pay 105 mln stg for Grampian.

text.p: Consolidation in Britain's ITV television network gained pace on Tuesday when its two main Scottish broadcasters Scottish Media Group Plc and Grampian Television Plc agreed to merge.
Scottish Media, which broadcasts to Glasgow, Edinburgh and central Scotland, said it would pay about 105 million pounds ($170 million) for Grampian, the ITV licence holder for northern Scotland.
The combined broadcasting group, which produced 1,350 hours of regional programming and 135 hours of network programming in 1996, will now cover over six percent of the total ITV advertising market.

Scottish Media has offered 18.3425 new Scottish Media shares and 192 pounds of new Scottish Media convertible unsecured loan stock for every 100 Grampian shares, it said. There will also be a full cash alternative to the offer of 320 pence per share.

Scottish Media, formerly Scottish Television, is emerging as a powerful force north of the border. It expanded from its original TV base with the acquisition of leading Glasgow newspapers the Herald and Evening Times for 120 million pounds last year.

The latest transaction marked further consolidation for the ITV commercial television sector since the two-licence ownership limit was removed and replaced by a cap of 15 percent of television audience last year.
Another ITV franchisee, Yorkshire-Tyne Television confirmed on Monday that it was in talks with Granada Group Plc about an offer by Granada for the shares in YTV it does not already own.
The deal between Scottish Media and Grampian, though relatively smaller, is expected to improve effectiveness and reduce costs for both groups.
It will also help ITV tackle burgeoning competition from development of digital and satellite broadcasting which threatens to reshape television viewing habits all over the UK.
Scottish Media's share price rose 7 1/2 pence to 706 while Grampian Television touched a new year's high of 317 1/2 pence.
Trade in Grampian's shares got a further boost with Scottish Media buying 3.26 million shares representing 9.9 percent in the target firm.
The merger with Grampian is expected to be earnings neutral for Scottish Media in the current financial year but is seen enhancing earnings in the first complete financial year following the merger.
"We have run the calculations on every possible scenario and they all indicate earnings enhancement," Scottish Media's managing director Andrew Flanagan told reporters.
He declined to specify how big the cost savings would be from the merger or how many jobs would be lost.
Both analysts and Scottish Media anticipate approval by the regulatory Independent Television Commission.
